column2: By the troubled year 316, during the Alexander Era, the Empire remained whole only in name, for Emperor Alexander had not appeared in public for years and rumors of his death spread unchecked. In his absence, nobles ruled as sovereigns, merchant princes bent trade to their will, generals gathered loyal armies, and secretive sorcerers whispered of darker designs. Imperial banners still flew above city walls, but unity was a memory, and intrigue now governed the realm where law and loyalty once stood.
